framework.reasoning: SCHEMA NOTE: this schema's framework.primary enum (pytorch/jax/tensorflow) assumes a neural-network paper and has no quantum-computing option. 'pytorch' above is a placeholder to satisfy the schema only -- it is NOT what this repo actually uses. The ACTUAL implementation framework is Qiskit + Qiskit Aer (with numpy for classical GF(2)/cipher reference code), matching the paper's explicit statement that it used 'the Qiskit framework [10, 11]' on real IBM hardware (Section 3.2). Qiskit Aer's statevector simulator stands in for the paper's proprietary 'QuantumOS on NVIDIA B200' simulator (Section 3.3), which is not publicly available. See requirements.txt / README.md for the real dependency set (qiskit, qiskit-aer, qiskit-ibm-runtime).

module_hierarchy.description: GF(2) Gaussian elimination utilities: build null-space basis from a set of linear constraint vectors.

Best-effort substitute for the paper's WITHHELD hardware-scaling technique (SIR ambiguities[0], confidence 0.05/0.45 for our substitute). Implements a top-K candidate-narrowing + classical-verification heuristic: rank candidate keys by how well they satisfy the collected (possibly noisy) Simon linear constraints, and report the true key's rank in that ordering. Explicitly NOT a reproduction of the paper's actual method, which is undisclosed.

module_hierarchy.description: Readout error-mitigation wrapper using Qiskit's published measurement-mitigation utilities (Nation et al. method, as cited). Standard/public technique only -- does NOT include the paper's withheld conditioning/post-selection technique.
Rank computation, birthday-bound comparison, and qubit-count/memory-ceiling utilities for reporting.
YAML config loading and RNG seeding for reproducible synthetic-key generation.

tensor_flows.name: Simon's algorithm end-to-end (Even-Mansour / CBC-MAC / Feistel)

output.name: recovered period s (or ranked candidates + true-key rank for the noisy hybrid regime)

steps: circuit = H^n |0> -> apply oracle_circuit -> H^n on input register        # Simon circuit skeleton
measurements = [] ; repeat shots times: sample circuit on backend -> collect measured bitstring y (y . s = 0)
IF noiseless/clean: solve_period(measurements, n) via GF(2) Gaussian elimination -> s directly (rank-1)

IF noisy hybrid regime (paper's n=6-10 real-hardware case): TopKHybridRanker.rank_candidates(...) -> {'rank': true_key_rank, ...}    # SIR ambiguities[0]/[2]: best-effort substitute for withheld technique

tensor_flows.name: Bernstein-Vazirani single-query readout
steps: apply oracle_circuit (f(x)=a.x via CNOTs into ancilla)
apply H^n on input register, measure -> a directly (single shot suffices, noiseless)

tensor_flows.name: Grover SPN key search
steps: repeat floor((pi/4)*sqrt(2^n)) times: apply oracle (phase-flip marked key) + diffuser
measure -> most frequent outcome = recovered key

risk_assessment.description: The paper's core real-hardware noise-scaling technique (enabling N=6-10 Even-Mansour recovery) is explicitly withheld pending an IP decision.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implemented a clearly-labeled best-effort substitute (TopKHybridRanker) and defaulted execution to a NOISELESS simulator, where the standard algorithms recover periods cleanly (rank-1) by construction -- this validates algorithmic correctness but explicitly does NOT reproduce the paper's noisy-hardware N=6-10 claim. README states this limitation prominently.

risk_assessment.description: Real IBM hardware (ibm_kingston) is not accessible from this environment.
risk_assessment.mitigation: backend/execution.py defaults to Qiskit Aer; a real-backend code path exists (qiskit-ibm-runtime) but requires the user to supply their own IBM Quantum API token.
